definition: A goal-oriented body of work that gathers related Stars and can be completed. The name evokes moving toward a star and the resulting blueshift in its observed frequencies.

An open-ended body of work that gathers related Stars, practiced indefinitely and never completed. Its Stars' completions reset at the start of each day. The name evokes receding from a star and the resulting redshift in its observed frequencies.

A tier of a Redshift or Blueshift: First, Second, Third, or Fourth Magnitude. First Magnitude is the highest, Fourth the lowest. A Star belongs to the Magnitude of its shift. Within a Magnitude, shifts are roughly equivalent and unordered.
A single, actionable piece of work belonging to one Blueshift or Redshift.
A Star of a Blueshift designated as current focus. North Star is a persistent designation: there is no limit on how many North Stars may exist at once.
The static site that documents the Polaris methodology: a Legend of concepts and Guides for working with them.
The canonical quick-reference of Polaris's concepts, wherever it appears.
A walkthrough in the Atlas of one part of the Polaris methodology.
